This tool utilizes an alignment insert in a central opening of the magnet to coaxially align fastener guide holes through polar plates or protective covers on opposing planar sides of the magnet and a fastener guide hole in the insert, whereby insertion of the fastener through the guide holes laterally aligns the components of the assembly. The invention is the release device/cap, that is part of the assembly by means of a self-adhering or hinged cap with a lip, square, circular or other shape, to aid in the separation of ferrous material from the magnetic tool by pushing away the cap from the magnetic hand tool by holding the lip for that purpose. The divots make it that the release lever device/cap is held onto the magnetic hand tool assembly. The separation allows for the ferrous material to fall in the drop collection box by ways of gravitational pull.

outputs.L4:
The magnetic hand tool is designed to collect ferrous objects such as nails, screws, washers, metal shavings, and other steel debris from floors, workbenches, soil, and similar surfaces. The tool includes a handle connected to a magnetic pickup assembly. Within the assembly, an alignment insert positions the magnet relative to one or more polar plates, protective covers, and a removable release cap. Fastener guide holes extending through the associated components maintain coaxial alignment during assembly and allow the parts to be secured reliably without shifting or damaging the magnet.

The release cap covers the material-collecting face of the magnetic assembly. Depending on the embodiment, the cap may be held against the assembly by magnetic attraction or may be attached by a hinge. A projecting lip provides an accessible gripping surface. During use, magnetic force passes through the cap and attracts ferrous objects to its exterior surface, allowing the user to sweep or place the tool over an area without directly handling sharp or contaminated debris.

To unload the tool, the user positions the magnetic assembly above a collection box, waste container, or sorting bin and pulls the cap away by its lip. Separating the cap and the collected material from the magnet rapidly reduces the magnetic holding force at the cap’s outer surface. The collected objects are therefore released and fall by gravity into the container. A hinged cap can then be swung back into its operating position, while a removable self-adhering cap can be placed against the magnetic assembly and retained by magnetic attraction.

This arrangement provides fast, controlled unloading without requiring the user to scrape debris from the magnet or remove individual objects by hand. It also helps protect the magnetic components from impact and wear, maintains proper alignment of the assembled parts, and improves safety when collecting sharp ferrous material. The result is a durable and convenient hand tool suitable for workshops, construction sites, manufacturing areas, garages, yards, and other locations where metallic debris must be collected and discharged efficiently.

counterfactuals.output: A magnetic hand tool for collecting and releasing ferrous objects includes a handle, an elongated support member, and a magnetic pickup assembly positioned near a distal end of the support member. A quick-release cap is disposed over at least a portion of the magnetic pickup assembly and provides an exterior collection surface on which ferrous objects are retained by magnetic attraction. The cap is selectively movable between a collection position adjacent the magnetic pickup assembly and a release position spaced from or displaced relative to the magnetic pickup assembly. In various embodiments, the cap is removably attached by a friction fit, detent, latch, threaded connection, or magnetic coupling, or is hingedly attached to the support member. counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention for sweeping metal debris from a surface using a magnet, alignment insert, polar plates, fastener guide holes, and a release cap with a gripping lip and retaining divots.
counterfactuals.output:
A magnetic sweeping device includes a housing containing a magnet positioned between opposing ferromagnetic polar plates. An alignment insert locates the magnet and polar plates within the housing, maintains their spacing, and directs magnetic flux toward a debris-collecting surface. Fastener guide holes extend through the alignment insert and correspond with holes in the polar plates and housing, ensuring accurate assembly and guiding fasteners without contacting or misaligning the magnet.

A removable release cap covers the debris-collecting surface. During use, magnetic attraction transmitted through the cap collects nails, filings, screws, and other ferrous debris. The cap includes an outwardly projecting gripping lip that allows a user to pull the cap away from the housing. Retaining divots on the cap releasably engage complementary projections or recesses on the housing or polar plates, holding the cap in place during sweeping. When the cap is removed, the collected debris is displaced away from the magnet and drops from the cap for convenient disposal.

counterfactuals.prompt: Rewrite my notes as a formal invention summary: a handheld magnetic pickup tool has coaxially aligned assembly components and a self-adhering cap that can be pushed away to release collected metal by gravity.
counterfactuals.output:
## Invention Summary

The invention relates to a handheld magnetic pickup tool configured to collect and release ferromagnetic objects. The tool includes multiple assembly components arranged in coaxial alignment to provide a compact and structurally efficient configuration. A self-adhering cap is removably retained at the collection end of the tool by magnetic attraction or another releasable holding force. During use, metallic objects are attracted to and collected at the cap. To discharge the collected objects, the cap is pushed away from the magnetic pickup region, reducing or eliminating the magnetic retention force and allowing the objects to fall from the cap under gravity. This arrangement enables convenient, controlled release without requiring the user to manually remove the collected metal objects.

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain the construction and operation of a magnetic collection tool whose central insert aligns the magnet, protective covers, and fastener, while a shaped lever cap enables quick removal of ferrous material.
counterfactuals.output:
A magnetic collection tool of this type is built as a compact, layered assembly:

- **Magnet:** Supplies the field that attracts nails, screws, chips, and other ferrous debris.
- **Central insert or hub:** Fits through or into the magnet and acts as the locating member. Its shoulders, bore, or mating surfaces keep the magnet concentric with the upper and lower protective covers and provide a controlled passage or seat for the fastener.
- **Protective covers:** Enclose the magnet’s faces and edges, preventing chipping, corrosion, and direct impact. The collection-side cover also provides a smooth surface from which debris can be removed.
- **Fastener:** Typically a screw, bolt, or rivet passing through the aligned components. Tightening it clamps the covers, magnet, insert, and cap into one unit without placing excessive localized stress on a brittle permanent magnet.
- **Shaped lever cap:** Mounted over the assembly and formed with a raised edge, ramp, lip, or pivoting profile. Besides protecting the upper side, it functions as a handle or lever for releasing collected material.

### Operation

When the tool is moved near ferrous objects, the magnet’s field passes through the collection-side cover and holds the objects against that surface. The insert maintains alignment, so the magnetic assembly remains stable and the clamping load is carried through the hub rather than directly through the magnet.

To empty the tool, the user actuates or tilts the shaped lever cap. Its geometry provides mechanical advantage and either lifts the magnetic assembly away from the collected material or separates the debris from the strongest part of the magnetic field. As the air gap increases, magnetic attraction drops rapidly, allowing the nails, filings, or other objects to fall off quickly. Returning the cap to its normal position restores the tool for collection.

The design therefore combines **accurate assembly, protection of the magnet, secure fastening, and tool-free debris release** in a single structure.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create patent language for a magnetic hand tool and assembly method featuring opposing plates, an alignment insert, lateral fastener alignment, and a detachable or hinged release device that deposits collected ferrous articles into a drop box.
counterfactuals.output:
## Title

**Magnetic Hand Tool With Aligned Plate Assembly and Article Release Device**

## Abstract

A magnetic hand tool includes first and second opposing plates, an alignment insert positioned between the opposing plates, and one or more magnetic elements supported by the plates. The alignment insert establishes spacing and relative positioning of the opposing plates and includes one or more laterally extending alignment passages positioned to register with corresponding fastener openings in the opposing plates. Fasteners extend laterally through the registered openings and passages to secure the assembly. A release device is movable relative to a magnetic collection region of the tool and is selectively detachable from, or hingedly connected to, the tool. Movement of the release device separates collected ferrous articles from the magnetic collection region, allowing the articles to fall into a drop box or other receptacle. Methods of assembling and operating the tool are also disclosed.

## Technical Field

The disclosure relates to magnetic pickup and collection tools and, more particularly, to a hand-operated magnetic tool having an aligned plate assembly and a movable release device for depositing collected ferrous articles into a receptacle.

## Summary

In one aspect, a magnetic hand tool includes a first plate, a second plate disposed opposite the first plate, and an alignment insert received between the plates. The insert maintains a selected spacing between the plates and aligns one or more fastening locations of the plates. At least one magnetic element is retained by, between, or adjacent to the plates to define a magnetic collection region.

The first plate, second plate, and alignment insert may include laterally aligned openings through which one or more fasteners are received. As used herein, “laterally” includes a direction extending transversely to a longitudinal axis of the tool or transversely across the spaced plates. The alignment insert may include bosses, channels, recesses, pins, tabs, shoulders, or other registration features that position the plates before insertion or tightening of the fasteners.

A release device is arranged adjacent to the magnetic collection region. In some embodiments, the release device is detachable from the plate assembly. In other embodiments, the release device is coupled to the plate assembly by a hinge and is movable between a collection position and a release position. Movement or removal of the release device causes ferrous articles collected by magnetic attraction to be displaced beyond an effective holding region of the magnetic element, whereupon the articles are deposited into a drop box positioned beneath or adjacent to the tool.

## Exemplary Detailed Description

A magnetic hand tool may include a handle connected to a magnetic head assembly. The magnetic head assembly includes a first plate and a second plate arranged in opposing, spaced relation. An alignment insert is positioned between the first and second plates. The alignment insert may comprise a polymeric, metallic, elastomeric, composite, or other substantially rigid body configured to establish the spacing and angular relationship of the opposing plates.

The alignment insert may include first and second plate-engaging surfaces and at least one transverse passage extending between opposite lateral sides of the insert. The first and second plates include respective fastener openings positioned in registration with the transverse passage. A fastener is inserted in a lateral direction through at least one of the plates and the alignment insert and is secured by a threaded opening, nut, clip, retainer, interference fit, or other fastening structure. Multiple transverse passages and fasteners may be used to inhibit translation or rotation of the plates relative to one another.

One or more permanent magnets, electromagnets, magnetically permeable pole pieces, or combinations thereof may be retained between the plates or mounted to an exterior surface of either plate. The plates may form pole extensions that concentrate magnetic flux at a collection surface of the head assembly.

A release device is positioned at or around the collection surface. The release device may comprise a sleeve, cover, tray, scraper, wiper, shield, ejector plate, or article-supporting member. In a collection position, ferrous articles are magnetically retained against or adjacent to the release device. To discharge the articles, the release device is moved away from the magnetic element, moved across the collection surface, pivoted relative to the plate assembly, or detached from the plate assembly. Such movement increases the distance between the articles and the magnetic element or mechanically wipes the articles from the collection surface, thereby reducing the magnetic holding force sufficiently for gravity to move the articles into a drop box.

In a hinged embodiment, the release device is connected to the head assembly by a hinge located along an edge of the release device. A latch may retain the release device in the collection position. Releasing the latch permits the release device to pivot to a discharge position over the drop box. The hinge may include a pin hinge, living hinge, flexible strap, ball-and-socket connection, or other pivotable coupling.

In a detachable embodiment, the release device may be retained by clips, tabs, magnets, sliding rails, a bayonet connection, a snap fit, or a releasable fastener. Separation of the release device from the head assembly carries or wipes the collected articles beyond the effective magnetic holding region so that the articles fall into the drop box.

The drop box may be a separate receptacle or may be removably supported by the tool. The box may include an open upper end positioned beneath a discharge path of the release device. Guides, stops, or docking features may establish a repeatable position between the head assembly and the drop box during discharge.

## Claims

1. **A magnetic hand tool comprising:**  
   a first plate;  
   a second plate disposed opposite the first plate;  
   an alignment insert positioned between the first plate and the second plate and configured to establish relative alignment of the first plate and the second plate;  
   at least one magnetic element supported by the first plate, the second plate, or the alignment insert and configured to generate a magnetic field at a collection region of the magnetic hand tool;  
   at least one fastener extending laterally through aligned portions of the first plate, the alignment insert, and the second plate; and  
   a release device movable relative to the collection region between a collection position, in which ferrous articles are retainable at the collection region by the magnetic field, and a release position, in which the release device causes the ferrous articles to move beyond an effective holding region of the magnetic field for deposit into a drop box.

2. The magnetic hand tool of claim 1, wherein the alignment insert includes a transverse passage aligned with a first fastener opening in the first plate and a second fastener opening in the second plate.

3. The magnetic hand tool of claim 1, wherein the at least one fastener extends in a direction transverse to a longitudinal axis of the magnetic hand tool.

4. The magnetic hand tool of claim 1, wherein the alignment insert includes at least one registration feature engaging a complementary feature of at least one of the first plate and the second plate.

5. The magnetic hand tool of claim 4, wherein the registration feature comprises a boss, pin, shoulder, recess, channel, tab, or combination thereof.

6. The magnetic hand tool of claim 1, wherein the at least one magnetic element is retained in a cavity defined at least partially by the first plate, the second plate, and the alignment insert.

7. The magnetic hand tool of claim 1, wherein the release device is detachably coupled to the magnetic hand tool.

8. The magnetic hand tool of claim 7, wherein the release device is detachably coupled by at least one of a clip, snap fit, sliding connection, magnetic connection, bayonet connection, or releasable fastener.

9. The magnetic hand tool of claim 1, wherein the release device is hingedly coupled to at least one of the first plate, the second plate, or the alignment insert.

10. The magnetic hand tool of claim 9, further comprising a latch configured to retain the release device in the collection position.

11. The magnetic hand tool of claim 1, wherein the release device comprises a cover, sleeve, scraper, wiper, tray, shield, or ejector plate positioned between the ferrous articles and the at least one magnetic element while the release device is in the collection position.

12. The magnetic hand tool of claim 1, wherein movement of the release device to the release position increases a separation distance between the ferrous articles and the at least one magnetic element.

13. The magnetic hand tool of claim 1, further comprising the drop box, the drop box having an opening positionable along a discharge path of the ferrous articles.

14. The magnetic hand tool of claim 13, wherein the magnetic hand tool or the drop box includes a docking feature configured to align the collection region with the opening of the drop box.

15. **A magnetic article collection system comprising:**  
   a magnetic pickup head including opposing plates, an alignment insert disposed between the opposing plates, and a magnetic element;  
   a plurality of laterally oriented fasteners securing the opposing plates to the alignment insert;  
   a release member detachably or pivotably coupled to the magnetic pickup head; and  
   a receptacle positionable beneath the release member,  
   wherein displacement of the release member relative to the magnetic pickup head releases collected ferrous articles from magnetic retention and directs the collected ferrous articles into the receptacle.

16. The magnetic article collection system of claim 15, wherein the release member is pivotable about an axis located along an edge of the magnetic pickup head.

17. The magnetic article collection system of claim 15, wherein the release member mechanically wipes the collected ferrous articles across or away from a magnetic collection surface.

18. **A method of assembling a magnetic hand tool, the method comprising:**  
   positioning an alignment insert between a first plate and an opposing second plate;  
   engaging the alignment insert with the first and second plates to establish a selected spacing and relative position of the first and second plates;  
   aligning a laterally extending passage of the alignment insert with respective fastener openings of the first and second plates;  
   inserting a fastener laterally through the aligned fastener openings and the laterally extending passage;  
   securing at least one magnetic element relative to the first and second plates to form a magnetic collection region; and  
   coupling a movable release device to the magnetic hand tool such that the release device is detachable from or pivotable relative to the magnetic collection region.

19. The method of claim 18, further comprising positioning a second lateral fastener through a second set of aligned openings to inhibit relative rotation of the first and second plates.

20. **A method of collecting and discharging ferrous articles, the method comprising:**  
   positioning a release device of a magnetic hand tool in a collection position adjacent to a magnetic collection region;  
   bringing the magnetic collection region sufficiently close to ferrous articles to magnetically retain the ferrous articles;  
   positioning the magnetic hand tool relative to a drop box; and  
   detaching or pivoting the release device relative to the magnetic collection region to reduce magnetic retention of the ferrous articles and deposit the ferrous articles into the drop box.

21. The method of claim 20, wherein detaching or pivoting the release device mechanically displaces the ferrous articles away from a magnetic element of the magnetic hand tool.

22. The method of claim 20, further comprising engaging a docking feature of the magnetic hand tool with a complementary docking feature of the drop box before detaching or pivoting the release device.

*This draft is general-purpose patent language and should be reviewed against the intended structure, drawings, prior art, and jurisdiction-specific filing requirements by qualified patent counsel.*
